newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Mitsui wins telecoms tender in Uzbekistan.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui wins telecoms tender in Uzbekistan.

text.p: Japan's Mitsui and Co Ltd has won an 11.3 billion yen ($97.4 million) tender to improve Uzbekistan's telecommunications system, an official statement said on Monday.

The statement, issued by the former Soviet republic's Communications Ministry, said Mitsui would purchase and deliver equipment necessary to install exchanges with a capacity of 251,000 lines in the Karakalpakstan, Bukhara, Navoi and Khorezm regions.
Mitsui will also provide the equipment for laying over 1,700 km (1,000 miles) of fibre-optic lines.
The statement said Mitsui should start work in the beginning of 1997.
The initial tendered sum of 12.7 billion yen represented a loan granted earlier to the Uzbek government by Japan's Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund.

Germany's Teleport Sachsen-Anhalt, another participant in the tender, has won the right to run and manage the systems provided by Mitsui but the statement gave no further details. ($ = 115.9 Japanese Yen)
